title: the build gate judges every component a ticket writes, not only its owner
intention: A ticket's PROVEME crossing runs the build_inspector over every census component holding a path in its bounds.in, not only the component its owning_intention names, so a red its build writes into another component reds its own crossing.
why: Measured 2026-11-18: dda0e72b9c67's build (cairn c9d4e79f6) added `from cairn.devices.tester.isolation import ...` at bin/proofs/test_a_proof_run_by_any_spelling_is_sealed.py:81, a path in its bounds.in. Its owning_intention is cairn/tools/scratch, so transitions._build_gate inspected only that directory; encapsulation_holds on the scratch row reds 0 of the breach (source 'bin', target 'cairn/devices/tester'), and dda0 crossed PROVEME and PROVED green. The red surfaced at the next bin-owned ticket, 78a600419a21, whose PROVED was refused and needed bug ticket 973ead3631e1.
traces_to: Law 8 (nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass): a gate that inspects one of the components a build wrote passes the rest unexamined. RULE 1: the breach is a reach into a device.
how: In cairn/tools/base/transitions.py _build_gate (inspect_build beneath it, transitions.py:1264), when the crossing carries a ticket, read its bounds.in (ticket_file.plans_of + read_ticket, as cross.py does), map each path to its innermost component with the same resolver encapsulation_breaches uses for a breach's source (so bin/ resolves to 'bin', which the cairn/ census does not list), run inspect_build over the owning component plus those, refuse on any red with each finding naming its component, and name every inspected component in the note and record. Red-first proof: a scratch repo with two components; a ticket owned by A whose bounds.in writes a cross-device import into B reds naming B.
constraints: a ticket whose bounds.in all sit in its owning component inspects exactly as today (one component, same record shape)
no sieve's own logic changes; only which census rows the gate runs them over
this does not answer Q#103 (open-212b2de5c6b8: one ticket per component, or one spanning ticket); it measures every component a ticket writes under either answer

outcomes.claim: a PROVEME crossing for a ticket owned by component A whose bounds.in holds a file in component B carrying a cross-device import is refused, the finding naming B's encapsulation_holds, nothing journaled
the same ticket with the import removed crosses, and the crossing's record names both A and B as inspected
